title: An endless stream of the dead follows the front, and stops when players stop
rule: Where the dead keep coming, use one maker with spawn points in small named groups along the way: each stage moves the stream to the next group, sets how many may be alive at once (6, then 8, then 4) and starts a 15 to 20 s timer that stops the stream if nobody moves on; moving on cancels the timer. Spawn only at points out of sight. When the stage's reason ends, stop the makers and send the living off to a spot out of sight, one a second, and remove them there. Progress, not time, brings the dead. Changing how our infestation spawns its zombies: ask the owner first.
why: d1_town_02a graveyard_zombie_maker: npc_template_maker MaxNPCCount 10000, MaxLiveChildren 6, SpawnFrequency 1, CriterionVisibility 1 (only points out of sight), DestinationGroup zombie_dest_group_1; 13 info_npc_spawn_destination in four groups of 3 or 4 (ReuseDelay 1). Each stage's trigger_once: ChangeDestinationGroup(zombie_dest_group_2, 3, then 4), Enable @0.2, SetMaxLiveChildren 8 then 4, Trigger its own cull relay @20 or @15 (whose one output is the maker's Disable), and CancelPending and Kill on the last stage's cull relay; the last stage also Disables @15. d1_town_02 cable car: stepping in Kills cavezombies_maker1 and 2 (6 each, 1 alive) and a 1 s logic_timer runs each fast zombie's away sequence (run to a spot, Kill there), a math_counter of 2 stopping it. Elsewhere 142 of the 154 makers in the six maps hold one NPC and are fired once by Spawn from a trigger_once (101 lines).
how: Gamemode (FindSpawnPos in sv_livingcity.lua, the cleanup jobs): zombies now come up at zspawn points or anywhere in a zone, unseen and 400 from players, with no cap tied to a job. Valve's way would give a cleanup crew a cap of 6 to 8 alive near it, pick spawn points from the cluster nearest the crew's next growth, go quiet when the crew has done nothing for 20 s, and at the job's end walk the zombies left near the crew off out of sight before removing them. Map modules: lc_zspawn points in clusters of 3 or 4, the clusters 300 to 900 apart along the quarter's way in.
check: review; a robot-player run of a cleanup job counting zombies alive near the crew (never over the cap)

title: Some of the dead lie slumped, and rise when someone comes near or hurts them
rule: Lay a few zombies slumped against walls and on floors (slump_a or slump_b) where people pass; each rises (slumprise_a, slumprise_a2, slumprise_b) when a player comes within about 100 to 400, looks at it, or hurts it, then goes for the nearest player. Rise them a fraction of a second apart, never all at once. In the dark, any body on the floor is a threat. Changes how our infestation's zombies appear: ask the owner first.
why: d1_town_01 and 01a: 17 scripted_sequences hold a zombie in slump_a (13) or slump_b (2) and play slumprise_a (11), slumprise_a2 (2) or slumprise_b (2); m_fMoveTo 4 (in place), spawnflags 624 (start on spawn 16, no interruptions 32, override AI 64, priority 512) or 608; a trigger_once fires BeginSequence, the zombie's own OnDamaged fires it too and Kills that trigger, and OnEndSequence > StartSchedule (set enemy to the player and run). Three rise @0.5, @1 and @1.3 (town_getup_06 to 08). d1_town_02: three more rise when the player looks at them (ai_script_conditions PlayerActorFOV 60 to 65 with line of sight), enabled 0.4 s after they are spawned.
how: Gamemode: a share of infestation zombies (the owner's call, say 1 in 5) spawned against a wall in the slump pose, held by a scripted_sequence as MakeSequence in sv_livingcity.lua does, and woken by a player within 300, a player looking at it within 60 degrees, or damage; neighbours woken 0.3 to 0.5 s apart. Check in game that the zombie models have these sequences. Map modules: lc_slump spots on the floor against the walls of the quarter's rooms.
check: review; a test that a slumped zombie wakes on damage and on a player within 300

title: A gas trap: open the valve, light it, shut it to put it out
rule: A fire trap is a gas valve and a way to light it. Turning the wheel lets gas hiss out (a loop and a heat haze); a press of the igniter, any fire close to the gas, or a shot or blast next to it lights it; a carpet of small fires then covers the gassed ground and sets alight whatever walks in; turning the wheel back puts it out, and it can be used again. Players burn as well as the dead: the wheel and the igniter stand outside the fire.
why: d1_town_01 zombiepyre, hallfire and zombiecage traps, wired alike. Wheel: func_door_rotating distance 180, speed 80, wait 9999; OnOpen: d1_town.GasJet loop (flag 16, radius 600), env_steam type 1 heat haze (Speed 120, StartSize 10, EndSize 20, JetLength 80, Rate 26), arms the light relay. Lighting: the igniter (func_door_rotating 90, wait 0.5, four clicks @0, 0.3, 0.6, 0.9 with env_spark), an env_firesensor (fireradius 39, heatlevel 1, HeatLevelStart), an env_microphone (MaxRange 100, Sensitivity 1, flags 40: bullet impacts and explosions, OnHeardSound). Lit: 40 env_fire over 274 by 234 (pyre) or 32 over 328 by 85 (corridor), nearest 8 to 14 apart, firesize 25 to 130, flags 3, fireattack 0.05, ignitionpoint 10; env_firesource fireradius 45, firedamage 100 (5 in the pyre); a trigger_hurt; d1_town.FlameTrapIgnite and d1_town.LargeFireLoop. Wheel shut: d1_town.FlameTrapExtinguish, ExtinguishTemporary(1) @0.5, the fires Disabled @2, the light off @0.5.
how: Map modules: a gas trap piece for the sealed quarter (lc_ravenholm.vmf) and the infestation's yards: a propane canister and a valvewheel002 wheel by a wall, a Firetrap_button01a igniter outside the gassed patch, the fire carpet as env_fire about 12 apart (fewer if the server's frame time suffers: test it). Gamemode, new: a growth or zombie burned in it counts for a cleanup job (the owner's call).
check: review; map_lint 'wire': a trap's env_fire start off and are Enabled and Disabled by name; an env_microphone has MaxRange and flags

title: The car on the rope drops on a lever and winds itself back up
rule: Hang a heavy wreck over a choke point where the dead gather; a lever drops it and stops it, the pulleys spin with a motor sound while it falls, it lands with a crash, and a winch lifts it back up so the next player can use it again; while it hangs, the rope creaks now and then.
why: d1_town_01 crushtrap_01 and 02: car004a_physics prop_physics (massScale 4) on a phys_lengthconstraint from an unseen func_physbox ballast on a phys_slideconstraint, in one phys_constraintsystem; a func_rot_button lever (distance 10, wait 4) toggles the drop relay (slide SetVelocity(10) or (8), d1_town.CarRelease and d1_town.CarTrapMotorLoop, func_rotating pulleys maxspeed 900 to 1200) and the stop relay (SetVelocity(0), re-arms the drop @2); a trigger_multiple of flag 8 (physics objects) filtered to the car's name at the bottom plays d1_town.CarHit and stops the pulleys, then a lift trigger reverses them (SetSpeed(500)); while it hangs a logic_timer (random 3 to 7 s) plays d1_town.CarStraining. The arena's three zombie makers fire @0, @0.5 and @1.
how: Map modules: a car trap piece over a lane or yard of the quarter (lc_ravenholm.vmf), its lever on a wall out of the drop; the winch makes it a trap for every player, not one use. Test the constraint system on a server (physics can jitter).
check: review; map_assets: the car is a physics model

title: A live fence shocks in pulses and throws you back, until someone cuts the power
rule: A charged fence or wire hurts in pulses, not as a steady drain: a jolt, a spark, a zap and a shove back, then a third of a second off. It stays live until someone finds the power box and switches it off, which opens the way on (a ladder, a gate). The step is to find and throw the switch, never to wait it out (house rule 9).
why: d1_town_01 electric_fence: trigger_hurt damage 10, damagecap 20, damagetype 256 (shock), flags 11; OnHurt: env_physexplosion, one of four Town.d1_town_01_LoudSpark sounds by logic_case PickRandom, env_spark @0, 0.1 and 0.3, Disable itself, and a logic_timer Enables it again @0.3; OnHurtPlayer: a trigger_push of speed 500 for 0.2 s. A transformer hum (radius 400) and an electric loop (radius 500) mark it. The power switch (tram_button) Kills the hurt and the pushes, breaks the hanging corpse's constraint and Enables func_useableladder electric_fence_ladder. (Its blue light flickers: not for us.) No electrified water in these six maps.
how: A new step for the sealed quarter's jobs (the flush squad, the Resistance shutting the sewer door): a live fence or flooded floor across the way, its power box hidden nearby; finding it is a hold-E search (LC.QuestSearchStage) and switching it off opens the way. The owner's call.

title: An ally sets off the trap, never with a player in it
rule: When an NPC ally sets off explosives or fire for the players (to block the dead, to clear the way), only the ally's shot counts, he aims at it only once he is at his post, and he stops while any player stands in the blast area. Our NPCs that use fire near players (the Cremator escort, soldiers with grenades) would follow the same rule: ask the owner first.
why: d1_town_02a propanetanks: an npc_bullseye (health 50) with damagefilter filter_multi (Grigori only, and not blast damage); the tanks themselves damagefilter filter_monk; ai_relationship monk hates the bullseye (rank 100) is applied 2 s after his assault point's OnArrival, reverted by trigger_multiple player_near_propanetanks_trigger OnStartTouch and applied again OnEndTouch. The bullseye's OnDeath runs the relay: env_explosion @0.2 and @0.4 (iMagnitude 100), env_shake, three env_fire (firesize 64, health 160) and two of 40, the tanks Break @0.4, scorch decals Activated @3, 5.5, 7 and 12, a light; Extinguish @47, the hold going on to @48 and @91. d1_town_01a: Grigori is given a bullseye behind each window to shoot through, Killed by the window's OnBreak.
how: Gamemode: before the Cremator (sv_livingcity_cremator.lua) or a soldier starts a fire or throws a grenade at a target, check no player is inside the blast radius; the target is the thing or the zombie, never the spot a player stands on. Changes how they fight: ask the owner.

title: Fast zombies are heard far off and glimpsed on the roofs before they come
rule: Before fast zombies attack, let players hear their call from far off, then glimpse one or two running over the roofs to a place out of sight where they are removed; the real attack comes a few seconds later. A sound and a glimpse instead of a warning line (house rule 10). For our infestation spreading from one district to the next: ask the owner first.
why: d1_town_02: 11 npc_fastzombie, 13 Town.d1_town_02_fz_alert_far1 (one-shot, radius 2500). first_fz_seq plays BR2_Roar with its call, then three more calls 1185 to 1589 away @0.5, 1.5 and 2; first_fz_a and _b, spawned @1 and @2, run (m_fMoveTo 2) to a spot and are Killed there on arrival (seven such runs in the map: roofs, the lift shaft, the cave); the freight lift's show: one in view with its call, two more @8 and @8.5. d1_town_02a's graveyard fast zombie makers play the call @2 after each spawn.
how: Gamemode: when a district's infestation leaks next door (sv_livingcity_districtinfest.lua) or a cleanup job starts, play a far fast-zombie call at the zone's edge and run one fast zombie across a roof or street to a hidden spot, removed there; no notice. Map modules: the quarter's roofs keep jump and climb nodes for the runs.

title: A climbing zombie is heard on the pipe
rule: Where the dead can climb (drainpipes, ladders up the houses), put an NPC-only trigger at the foot and at the top: as one climbs, the pipe clanks and shakes a little, so players hear it coming. Climbing routes open by script when the attack starts.

how: Map modules: the sealed quarter's drainpipes get climb nodes, the two NPC-only triggers with a metal clank, and a short pipe on a small rotating door to shake. Check in game that fast zombies use climb nodes from our .ain.

title: Crows lift ahead of a player and fly into the place he is going
rule: Leave crows on the ground and on the dead where the infestation starts; as a player comes they lift a second or two apart and fly ahead into the overrun place, where they are quietly removed out of sight. The way in is shown by birds, not text. For our infested districts: ask the owner first.

how: Gamemode: our birds (BIRDS in sv_livingcity_survival.lua) could gather on the edges of infested districts and lift into the zone when a player comes near, removed out of sight. Map modules: crow perch and fly-to hints in the quarter.

title: Spent headcrab canisters stay stuck in the ground, open
rule: Show that a place was shelled with a few spent headcrab canisters left stuck nose-down in lanes, yards and roofs, open and empty, rather than live headcrabs beside them. Our shelling's canisters go after 180 s: keeping some longer in the infested quarter is the owner's call.

No env_headcrabcanister in the six maps.
how: Map modules: 3 or 4 headcrabcannister01b props (prop_dynamic, DefaultAnim idle_open, pitch -45) in lc_ravenholm.vmf's lanes and yards. Gamemode: sv_livingcity_shelling.lua removes its wreckage at FLIGHT + 180 s; in the sealed quarter it could stay until cleaned up (ask).

Ravenholm (d1_town_01, 02): 7 ai_script_conditions wake a slumped zombie or start Grigori's scene when the player looks: PlayerActorFOV 60 to 65 (45 for Grigori) with line of sight, or PlayerTargetFOV 75 at the zombie's spot; d1_town_01's are Enabled only by another zombie's OnFoundPlayer, so the house wakes once one zombie has seen you.

Ravenholm: Grigori's gate nag is a logic_timer (RefireTime 20, StartDisabled 1) starting three nag scenes @0, 7 and 13, Enabled 1 s after his gate sequence begins and Killed with all three scenes by the trigger_once the player reaches (d1_town_02a); in d1_town_01 his voice goes ahead as three rant sounds placed 387 to 936 ahead of their triggers, each trigger stopping the last; no env_hudhint in the six maps.

Ravenholm's holds are timed by a slow machine players can see and hear: the freight lift climbs 385 at speed 12 (about 32 s) while fast zombies spawn at the button press, @1, and through the windows @5; the cable car's motor starts 45 s after Grigori's guard line and the car needs about 20 s more (784 at speed 40) while two makers of 6 send one fast zombie at a time along one of two routes (logic_case PickRandom); Grigori's propane fire holds the way for 47 s. For our flush job, the gate's own slow opening and motor sound can be the clock.

Ravenholm: Grigori's fights are heard before they are seen: d1_town_02 plays a zombie @1, shotgun @1.5, 2.4, 4.2 and 5, a mad laugh scene @3 and a zombie @3.5, 521 from the trigger; d1_town_01a a shotgun pair @0 and @0.75 with a window shattered.
